document.abstract: In this paper I want to summarize the present situation of the various newly introduced broadcast quality video recording systems using tapes of one-inch width. Further announcements and introductions of new recording equipment will certainly take place in the months ahead, and no attempt at prophesy is intended. It does not require a prophet, however, to see that changes are in store for most of us who use video recorders. The familiar, sometimes loved, sometimes hated quadruplex recorder is facing competition from a variety of systems now available to the television broadcaster. We can expect that quadruplex recordings will be with us for some time to come, though, and such recordings remain the standard for the national and international exchange of television programs.

authors.affiliation: Broadcasting Service University of Michigan Ann Arbor, Michigan
authors.bio: Frederick M. Remley is Technical Director for University of Michigan-Broadcasting Service, a position he has held since 1954. Fred is a member of both the Public Broadcasting System Engineering Committee and of Sub-Group G-2 (Video Recording) of the European Broadcasting Union Working Party G. On the subject of video recording, Fred is U.S. Delegate to meetings of CCIR and IEC TC-60. He has served in this capacity for CCIR since 1965, and for IEC since 1969. Mr. Remley has been active with SMPTE since 1966, when he became Chairman of the Video Tape Recording Committee. He maintained this position until 1970, when he became Chairman of the SMPTE Standards Committee, a role he filled until 1974. From 1975 to the present day, Fred has been Chairman of the SMPTE Committee on New Technology; and in 1977 he was Chairman of the SMPTE Working Group on One-Inch Continuous-Field Helical Video Recorders.
